Security Design: Waypoint Customer Data Protection

Every job carries Customer Contact Info, the information entity holding a customer's name, address, and phone number. We tag it with the Sensitive Data Classification, a data classification that governs the Customer Contact Info, governs the Job Record secure resource it lives on, and requires the Field Encryption Countermeasure. The Customer Contact Info is constrained by that same Sensitive Data Classification.

How long we keep it is the Ninety-Day Retention Policy, a security retention policy that constrains the Customer Contact Info and governs the Access Audit Config we use to prove compliance. The Access Audit Config, an audit config, monitors the Job Record, depends on the Ninety-Day Retention Policy to know how far back its trail must reach, triggers the Access Audit Evidence produced on every access, and mitigates the Credential Theft Threat by making misuse visible.

The Credential Theft Threat, a threat, targets the Customer Contact Info and accesses the Job Record when it succeeds; it aggregates the Field Encryption Countermeasure raised against it. The Field Encryption Countermeasure, a countermeasure, protects the Job Record, mitigates the Credential Theft Threat, requires the Access Audit Evidence to show it is in force, and fulfills the Data Residency Constraints, the security constraints that keep encrypted customer data in-region. The Access Audit Evidence, an evidence record, realizes the Access Audit Config and mitigates the Credential Theft Threat.
